chat_messages.text: Remind me why we went with rank fusion instead of just adding the scores?

Because the lexical ts_rank_cd scores and the vector cosine scores live on totally different scales, so a weighted sum needs calibration that drifts. RRF only looks at rank position, so it sidesteps that.
And k=60?
k=60 is the common default from the original RRF paper; it damps the contribution of low-ranked items without tuning per query.
If I run ingest twice does it double everything?
No — each turn gets a content_hash and the insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the second run reports everything as skipped.
What about editing a note then re-ingesting?
Edited text hashes differently, so it comes in as a new turn; the old one stays unless you clear it. We don't diff-update in place yet.
Can you catch me up on where the hiring thread landed?

Summarising the thread: Luke said we should hire at the senior level (L5), not mid, because a senior engineer can own the retrieval work end to end and we'll move faster even though it costs more up front.
Did anyone push back?
Dana worried about budget, but the group leaned toward Luke's view given how central retrieval is this quarter.
Where is the time going on a query?
Mostly the answer generation — parse and embed are tens of milliseconds, search and fuse are small, and the LLM answer dominates TTFT because retrieved turns go in the system prompt.
So we can't stream before retrieving?
Right, there's a data dependency: the facts have to be in the prompt before the first token, so retrieval blocks generation.
Could we ingest voice memos as a surface too?
Yes — surface is already a filter dimension ('text' | 'voice' | 'notes'), so transcribed voice memos would ingest as surface=voice and be filterable.
What's our compute budget looking like for Q3?
Q3 is mostly embedding API credits and a small Postgres host; the number firmed up later, but early Q3 it was comfortable.
